body_markdown:
Breaking new ground for Bentley is the Torcal–an 876-hp electric SUV, that uses the bones of the[Porsche Cayenne](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-porsche-cayenne-electric-specs-features-pictures-pricing/) .


The name Torcal comes from the rugged limestone landscape of *El Torcal de Antequera* in Spain, but Bentley could just as well have flipped it and called it the All-Torc as its 996 lb-ft of torque is the highest ever achieved from a car with a Flying B badge.


All that oomph comes from a pair of permanent magnet synchronous motors, each with a dry sump and filled with oil for a lifetime of running. It’s all-wheel-drive, of course, and at the front there’s an open differential, but the rear motor has a locking diff with a multi-plate clutch for each output shaft.


The battery capacity is 113 kWh, courtesy of 192 individual lithium-ion pouch cells, and the system runs on 800 volts. That should mean more than 300 miles of range, once EPA ratings are confirmed. Those charges will be quick, too. Hooked up to a 400V rapid charger a 10-80 percent charge can be achieved in 16 minutes, or 100 miles added in just seven minutes. Bentley is backing its battery with a ten-year or 100,000-mile warranty.


The Torcal is also the first Bentley to run fully active suspension, with two-valve dampers for what the company calls a “magic carpet” ride. Instead of conventional anti-roll bars there the reactive dampers deliver infinitely adjustable anti-roll torque.[Rear-wheel steering](https://www.hagerty.com/media/maintenance-and-tech/four-wheel-steering-is-having-its-moment-again/) is also installed to aid agility.


Carbon-ceramic brakes are an option to replace the standard steel items, and, should you decide to deploy all the torque of the Torcal to hit 60 from a standstill in 2.8 seconds, you might well wish to specify them to slow down again. It’s a hefty thing the Torcal, tipping the scales at almost 6000 pounds. Those racy figures are for the S version, while the entry-level Torcal will offer 810 hp and 881 lb-ft of twist.


Accompanying the performance is what Bentley calls Dynamic Symphony, which is a digital soundtrack created using real instruments including drums, a viola, and bass guitar that rises from a resting pulse to a crescendo as you accelerate. It’s played out through a 620-watt, 16-speaker audio system, or an optional 28-speaker Naim setup with Dolby Atmos, seat shakers, and headrest speakers. These sounds combine with interior lighting and the climate control and instrumentation to form four different drive modes: Bentley, Comfort, Sport, and Refresh to suit your mood and driving style.


Bentley


Bentley


It goes without saying that the cabin is ridiculously luxurious, with wood and aluminum, leather and Merino Wool all in plentiful supply. There’s a sizeable center screen and digital instrument panel, but also physical switches for important stuff like climate control and drive modes.


The Torcal’s interior is both similar to and distinctly different from the Porsche Cayenne Electric with which it shares its PPE architecture. When it comes to the exterior design, it’s only really by looking at the roofline and lower doors that you can tell that the two are connected. The Bentley out-blings the Porsche with its massive jewel-like grille, 22-inch multi-spoke alloys, its wider, squarer arches, and design nods to both the classic Continental T and the EXO 15 concept car.


Like it or not, it’s unmistakably a Bentley, and starting at around $230,000, it’s certainly priced like a Bentley. Whether it drives like one, we’ll have to wait and see.
